headline: Indonesia's SM+ has agreed to buy five business data centres from Princeton Digital Group, which says it will keep its focus on very large cloud-scale data centres.
score_reason: Pool 4 kept: the full text was read; the sale is signed by both sides but small in scale, with no price or completion date given.
importance_line: What changed is that one company is selling its smaller business-customer data centres to concentrate on very large ones, which matters first to Indonesian businesses that rent data-centre space, then to the two companies, and the doubt is that the report gives no price or completion date, and a signed agreement is not a finished deal.
source: ET Datacenters, citing SM+ and Princeton Digital Group
summary: ET Datacenters reports that PT SMPlus Digital Investama (SM+), an Indonesian digital-infrastructure company, announced a definitive agreement to buy Princeton Digital Group's enterprise data-centre business in Indonesia, five working facilities in Greater Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya and Pekanbaru, which would take SM+ to 31 sites in 25 Indonesian cities. Princeton Digital Group's chief operating officer says the sites were bought as part of an 'enter-and-expand' strategy and that the company will keep building its hyperscale portfolio, very large data centres for the biggest cloud customers, now about 400 megawatts in Indonesia; the report gives no price or completion date.
notes: Read in full: the plain-text fulltext copy was empty, so the article body was taken from the page's own embedded data (HTTP 200, not blocked). Status CONFIRMED because both companies announced the deal and are quoted; no price or closing date is stated. The 'hyperscale' gloss is ours.
